criteria.criterion: Avoids a universal rule and frames a decision
criteria.evidence: "The team lead is right about the direction and the fearful colleagues are right about the method. Don't delete the cron job this week, and don't leave it untouched." The response also sets out options A–D with gates and decision rights.

criteria.criterion: Requires the workaround record fields (owner, scope, side effects, detection, exit)
criteria.evidence: The 'Owner, review trigger, exit condition' section asks to "Name one person" and gives an exit condition. Detection is item 6 ("Write down a measurable definition of 'stale lease'"). Side effects are item 2. Scope appears in the canary section, and there is a decision record draft. The fallback says to "document it with an owner, a detection criterion and a review date".

criteria.criterion: Proposes bounded testing of removal with detection and rollback
criteria.evidence: "Canary: Disable the cron entry on one network node, or one AZ...". It also defines a stop condition ("Any stale-lease detection...") and a rollback ("Re-enable the cron job and restart the agent on that node"), and rolls out in stages.
Option B: "It stays accidental architecture and will surprise the next upgrade. The nightly restart is itself a risk." The fallback adds: "it becomes intentional rather than accidental".

criteria.criterion: Applies the 'risk introduced vs risk removed' test
criteria.evidence: "The workaround test (it is safe only while the risk it adds stays smaller than the risk it removes) can't be passed today because the risk it removes was never quantified."

critical_errors.error: recommends removing it across all nodes immediately without detection or rollback
critical_errors.evidence: Option A (remove everywhere this week) is rejected because it fails the evidence gate. The response recommends a canary on one node first.

critical_errors.error: recommends keeping it indefinitely without owner or review
critical_errors.evidence: Option B is rejected because it has "No owner and no exit condition". Even the fallback requires an owner, a detection criterion and a review date.

summary: The response passes all five criteria and commits neither critical error. It rejects both universal rules and frames the choice as a decision with options, gates, an owner and an exit condition. It proposes a one-node canary with detection, a stop condition and rollback. It names the job as accidental architecture and applies the 'risk introduced vs risk removed' test explicitly. It makes no book citations and invents nothing about the user's environment: causes are labelled as hypotheses and missing facts are listed as gaps.
